title: [Chapitre] IX et IX bis. [Ateliers] : notes manuscrites (05-15/07/1986).

errors: Excluding minimal a from M_1^- (and maximal a from M_1^+) correctly avoids empty rays.
The heuristic 'X < a for X ∈ M' is only informal; the formal content is the boundary/support definitions and the extended ≤̊.
Keeping I_{<a} distinct from I_{ω_0,a} despite equal supports is a deliberate choice; it is made explicit on the next page and is not an inconsistency.

ideas.what: Adjoin half-infinite 'interval' cells I_{<a}, I_{>a}, each with a single boundary point, to the combinatorial complex of points and bounded intervals of an ordered set L.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset of a point arrangement on the line (rays as unbounded 1-cells); ends/compactification of a 1-dimensional cell complex
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard in hyperplane-arrangement and oriented-matroid combinatorics (Zaslavsky 1975; Björner–Las Vergnas–Sturmfels–White–Ziegler)

ideas.what: Motivation: the complement Φ' of a (generalized) polygon has exactly the same boundary as Φ (δΦ = δΦ'), which fails without rays because of the extremal points ω_0, ω_1.
ideas.modern_name: Complementary chains with equal boundary in the line; discrete Alexander/Poincaré-type duality on R

ideas.what: Define support |I_{<a}| = L_{≤a}, interior L_{<a}, boundary {a}, and extend the face relations ⊴, ◁ to the enlarged set M̂.
ideas.modern_name: Closed/open cell supports in a regular cell (or poset) structure

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine technical step inside the unpublished 1986 'ateliers' formalism: adding unbounded rays so that complementation preserves boundaries. The construction itself is standard (arrangement face posets). Only its place in Grothendieck's combinatorial 'figures/ateliers' programme is of archival interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 more likely reads 'Φ, Φ', et non seule[ment]...' (with a superscript 5 above, probably a note marker) rather than 'et nous serons'.
Line 3 begins with a struck word followed by 'l'introduction des I_{<a}, I_{>a} ...'; the struck word appears to be 'donc'/'donne', not a clean 'donc'.
The crossed-out portion in the ∂I_{<a} line is 'δI_{>a} = δI_{<a}'-like scribbling; the retained statement is ∂I_{<a} = δI_{<a} = {a}.
Near the end: 'On notera quelquefois ◁ = ≤̊ [or ⊴ = ≤̊], en écrivant les nouveaux cas de ≤̊, indiquant I_{<a}...'; the symbol before '=' is missing in the machine transcription.
